Gate to gate checklist

The checklist takes the Istanbul local flight into a full flight simulator or a desktop sim, from a cold and dark gate back to the gate, with photos of the real cockpit and every MCDU entry of the trainer. On that flight each phase of the guide below links to its section, and your ticks stay in this browser.

The trainer

The trainer flies the whole Istanbul local flight in a working A320 cockpit, from cold and dark at the stand to the landing and back to the gate, and teaches this MCDU key by key on the way, with every switch, knob and lever around it. This page is the MCDU practice for other flights: the MCDU and the navigation display only, for any pair of airports in Istanbul or South Florida.

What is simulated

The FMGC pages used for a normal flight: INIT A and B, F PLN with lateral and vertical revisions, DEPARTURE and ARRIVAL with approach vias, DIR TO, PERF for every phase, RAD NAV, PROG, FUEL PRED, SEC F PLN and the DATA pages. The aircraft flies the managed profile, so you can watch the predictions come true on the navigation display. Fly by waypoints are flown with turn anticipation, so the path rounds each corner, as on the aircraft.

Choosing a flight

Change flight opens the airport list. For the airports you choose, the trainer picks the runways for the wind of the day, then the SID, STAR and approach that join up best, the cruise level and the fuel. Where a SID or a STAR ends in radar vectors, ATC clears you direct in flight and the simulation waits for your DIR TO. ILS approaches end in an automatic landing; RNAV approaches are flown in FINAL APP.

The simulated air is calm: the wind you enter on PERF APPR only sets VAPP. The alternate is planned as a direct leg. Line select keys are named by row and side, 1L to 6L on the left and 1R to 6R on the right.

Choose the flight

Pick where you leave from and where you land. The trainer plans the runways for the wind, the procedures that join up, the cruise level and the fuel. You can choose another runway or approach.

How to use this checklist

This takes an A320 from a cold and dark gate at Istanbul Airport (LTFM), around a short IFR loop over the Black Sea (108 NM, about 24 minutes in the air), and back to the same gate, one switch at a time. A330 changes are in their own section near the end. Plan on about 2 hours the first time.

It follows the real Airbus normal procedures, so it works in a full flight sim and in study level desktop sims (Fenix A320, FlyByWire A32NX, iniBuilds A330). Software versions move some fields to a different line key; when that happens, look for the same label on the page.

The flight in five parts

PartSectionsTimeWhat happens
At the gate1 to 445 to 60 minSet up the sim, power the aircraft, set the switches, program the MCDU
Leaving the gate5 to 720 to 40 minPush back, start both engines, taxi to runway 35L
In the air8 to 11about 18 minTake off, climb to FL150, cruise for 3 minutes, descend
Landing12 to 14about 6 minFly the ILS to 35R and land, or go around and try again
Back to the gate15 and 1615 to 30 minClean up, taxi in, park, shut down

First time? Read the short topics below and the Ground school once, practice in the trainer, then fly the sections in order. Every numbered section opens with one line on what it does and a Done when line: the state to reach before you move on. Stuck? The Beginner traps table near the end has the usual fixes.

Practice the MCDU first

The A320 Trainer flies this exact flight in your browser, in a working cockpit from cold and dark to the gate, with the same route, weights and speeds. One run through it makes section 4 familiar before you sit in the sim.

  1. Open the trainer and press Watch the flow: the whole flight is flown for you, step by step, from cold and dark to the stand. In section 4 the MCDU tab comes up and every entry is typed key by key.

  2. Press New flight and fly it yourself with the steps beside the cockpit: it asks where to start, the weather, the load and how much help you want. Yellow marks the control to use next; on the MCDU tab the key to press next lights up, and each step says why the entry matters.

  3. Then fly it again with Point at the next control cleared: each section counts the actions you did on your own.

  4. In your sim, make the same entries from section 4. Every value on the flight card matches the trainer.

The trainer codes no SID or STAR and builds its own approach points, CF35R and FF35R. Your sim's database differs there: section 4 says what changes, and the section Next step: real Istanbul procedures, near the end, covers the published routes.

Overhead light logic (the most useful thing to learn first)

  • No light on a pushbutton means normal. This is the Airbus "lights out" idea: after preparation the overhead should be dark.

  • White OFF means a crew member switched it off. Very few buttons should show this.

  • Blue ON means something that is normally off is now on (APU MASTER SW, APU BLEED, EXT PWR).

  • Green AVAIL means ready to use (APU running, ground power connected).

  • Amber FAULT means a problem. A few are normal before the engines run; the steps say which.

  • Anything under a guard or a red cover (IDG, RAT, DITCHING, fire AGENT buttons) stays untouched on a normal flight.

Scan for anything that is not dark, then ask why it is lit. An unexpected light is your cue to read the ECAM.

FCU knobs: push or pull

  • Push a knob = managed. The FMS flies what you built in the MCDU, and a dot lights beside that window (SPD and HDG also show dashes).

  • Pull a knob = selected. The aircraft flies the number in the window.

  • While in managed mode, turning a knob only previews a number; pull to use it. While in selected mode, turning changes the target directly.

  • The ALT knob is special: turning it sets the target altitude, but the aircraft only climbs or descends after you push (managed) or pull (selected) it.

MCDU basics

  • Type on the keypad. Text appears in the scratchpad, the bottom line of the screen.

  • Press the line select key (LSK) beside a field to put the scratchpad text into it. Keys are called 1L to 6L down the left and 1R to 6R down the right.

  • Amber boxes must be filled. Blue fields can be changed. Green values are computed. Magenta marks a speed or altitude constraint. Yellow is a temporary change that waits for INSERT.

  • CLR deletes one character; hold it to clear the scratchpad. To delete a field or waypoint, press CLR once (scratchpad shows CLR), then press that line's LSK.

  • The slash key separates two values in one field, for example ZFW/ZFWCG.

  • The up and down arrows scroll a list. NEXT PAGE moves to the next page of the same function.

  • FORMAT ERROR or NOT ALLOWED in the scratchpad means the entry was refused. Press CLR and retype.

How the steps are written

  • Switch and button names are in capitals, as printed in the cockpit.

  • A tick box is something you do. "Check" means look, do not change.

  • Weights, fuel, speeds and waypoints match the trainer flight. If your sim's EFB or load sheet gives other values, use those.

  • A dotted underline marks an abbreviation: point at it, or tap it on a phone, to see what it means. A yellow bar marks your next step, and Continue at the top takes you there. Click a picture to see it large.

Flight card

The example column is the trainer flight: off 35L, a loop through GINLI, ERTAS, BKZ and IST at FL150, then the ILS to 35R. That is 108 NM in about 24 minutes. Fill in the Yours column before touching a switch; every line is used later.

Most of the loop is climb and descent: the cruise at FL150 lasts about 3 minutes, from the top of climb after GINLI to the top of descent around ERTAS.

Why those runways: about 80% of the time the wind blows from the Black Sea, so Istanbul runs north flow: departures on 35L and 36, arrivals on 34L and 35R, plus some arrivals on 36 at peak times. 16L/34R is mostly a backup. The 17/35 pair sits just west of the terminal, so departing 35L and landing 35R keeps the taxi short. Field elevation is 325 ft.

Runway positions and use: Spotterguide, updated June 2026 and Wikipedia. Taxiway names and gate positions are not marked; take them from a real chart.

Sources: A320 Trainer (route, weights, speeds), IVAO Turkey LTFM briefing (runway use, point merge, approach altitudes), BA Virtual LTFM brief (inner runways for departures, outer for arrivals), AIP ILS 35R chart excerpt (12,000 ft transition altitude, ATIS), SkyVector LTFM (ATIS frequencies).

Cockpit map

Learn it in the order you will scan it: overhead columns, then glareshield, main panel and pedestal. Every step below names the panel it lives on.

Ground school

Read this part once before the first flight. Each topic explains one screen, panel or idea, mostly with a real photo whose numbers match the list under it; the numbered sections after it only tell you what to do. The photos come from different aircraft and flights, so take the values to set from the text, not from the photo.

How the A320 thinks: three ways to fly it

  1. By hand: sidestick and thrust levers. The fly by wire computers turn your stick into a flight path and protect you from stalling, overspeeding or over banking.

  2. Selected: you tell the autopilot a number on the FCU (a heading, an altitude, a speed) by pulling a knob. The aircraft flies that number.

  3. Managed: you build the whole route and profile in the MCDU, then push the FCU knobs. The FMS flies it, including SID and STAR constraints.

You will use all three on this flight. The FMA at the top of the PFD always tells you which one is active.

Learning path

  1. Session 1, in the browser, in the A320 Trainer: watch the flight once with Watch the flow, then fly it yourself, first with its pointer, then without. Its speed buttons run the long waits faster than real time.

  2. Session 2, on the ground: sections 1 to 4 only. Power up, set the overhead, program the MCDU with the trainer's entries. Repeat until you can do it without reading every line.

  3. Session 3: start, taxi, take off and climb to FL150. Stop the sim at the top of climb, about 8 minutes after takeoff.

  4. Session 4: approaches and landings only. A full flight sim can put you on final from the IOS; most desktop sims have a start or reposition on approach option. Do three autolands, then hand fly.

  5. Session 5: the whole flight, gate to gate, with this checklist open beside you.

The whole flight at a glance

Each number is a moment where you change something. Between them the autopilot and autothrust fly, and your job is to watch the FMA and get ready for the next number.

Reading the PFD

The PFD (primary flight display) is the screen right in front of you. Look at it more than anything else.

  • Scan pattern: FMA first, then attitude, speed, altitude, back to the FMA. Do it every few seconds when something changes.

  • On the real PFD the target speed triangle and the ILS diamonds are magenta, the FCU altitude is cyan, and the yellow marks are your own aircraft.

  • The photo shows a descent: MACH, V/S 1000 ft/min down with ALT armed in blue, and NAV. The trainer climb shows THR CLB, CLB toward FL150 and NAV instead.

The speed tape

  • Flap rule in one line: extend the next step only below the amber =, retract the next step only above F (for 1) or S (for 0).

  • On the takeoff roll the tape also shows V1 as a blue 1; V2 is the target triangle until acceleration.

  • With autothrust on and managed speed, the aircraft flies the triangle and stays between VLS and VMAX on its own.

The FMA, phase by phase

The FMA has five columns: 1 thrust, 2 vertical, 3 lateral, 4 approach capability and minimum, 5 what is engaged (AP1, AP2, 1FD2, A/THR). Line 1 is what is happening now (green), line 2 is armed and waiting (blue, or magenta when it comes from an FMS constraint). A box around a new mode means it just changed. Call each change out loud.

Reading the ND

The ND (navigation display) sits beside the PFD. Use ARC mode in flight, PLAN mode to check the route on the ground, and range 10 for taxi.

  • On the real ND the DECEL point and constraint circles are magenta, the next waypoint is white and the rest of the route is green.

  • During taxi, GS at the top left is your taxi speed; keep it under 20 kt.

  • A route line that suddenly ends means a F PLN DISCONTINUITY: the aircraft will fly straight on.

ECAM: the two centre screens

ECAM watches every system for you. The upper screen shows engines, fuel, flaps and messages; the lower screen shows one system page at a time.

  • Colours: green is normal, blue is an action still to do, amber is a caution (single chime), red is a warning (repeating sound, red MASTER WARN light on the glareshield).

  • When a message appears: read it, do the blue lines it lists from top to bottom, then press CLR. Press STS afterwards to see what is still affected.

  • Press MASTER WARN or MASTER CAUT (glareshield, in front of each pilot) to stop the sound and the flashing light.

FCU and EFIS panel

  • Dashes and a dot in a window mean managed: the FMS supplies that value. A number means selected: the aircraft flies your number.

  • The right seat has its own EFIS panel with the same controls; set both BARO knobs every time you change the altimeter.

  • Leave the top row buttons in their default state for this whole flight (knots, HDG V/S, feet).

MCDU keys

  • Every MCDU entry is the same two moves: type into the scratchpad, press the line key beside the target field. A prompt with a star (INSERT*, CONFIRM*) is pressed the same way.

  • A prompt with an arrow beside it (such as DEPARTURE or RETURN) only opens another page. Nothing changes in the flight plan until you press a star prompt such as INSERT.

  • Two MCDUs show the same FMS. Use the left one; the right one is the first officer's.

Thrust levers and autothrust

Airbus thrust levers do not move by themselves. You put them in a detent and the autothrust computer sets the actual thrust.

In a desktop sim, map the detents in the aircraft's EFB or settings so your hardware lever clicks into TOGA, FLX/MCT, CL and IDLE at the right places.

Flying by hand: what the sidestick does

The A320 is fly by wire: the sidestick asks for a change, the computers make it happen and then hold it. Fly with fingertips, not your fist: small input, let go, watch, correct again.

  • Pitch: stick back or forward asks for the nose to go up or down. Let go and the aircraft keeps its current flight path and trims itself.

  • Roll: stick sideways asks for a roll rate. Let go and the bank angle stays where it is, up to 33°. Beyond 33° it rolls back to 33° when you let go.

  • Turns are coordinated for you; the rudder pedals are for the ground and for crosswind.

  • Protections (normal law): bank stops at 67°, pitch at 30° up and 15° down, and the aircraft will not let you stall or overspeed. Near the stall, alpha floor even adds full thrust by itself.

  • Flare: below about 50 ft the aircraft slowly lowers the nose, like a conventional aircraft would. That is why you must pull gently to flare.

  • On the ground the stick moves the surfaces directly, which is why you hold half forward stick early in the takeoff roll.

  • Pitch trim is automatic in flight. You only set it by hand on the ground, for takeoff, with the trim wheel.

1. Sim setup

Start cold and dark at your LTFM gate with fuel, payload and ground power ready, and the takeoff numbers already on the flight card.

2. Power up from cold and dark

Next: 3. Cockpit preparation

3. Cockpit preparation

Sweep the overhead column by column, top to bottom, then the main panel, the pedestal and the glareshield. Goal: a dark overhead; only the blue ON lights (EXT PWR, APU MASTER SW, APU BLEED, RCDR GND CTL), the green APU AVAIL and the amber GEN 1 and GEN 2 FAULT lights stay lit, plus white ALIGN while the IRs align.

Done when: the IR knobs are at NAV, the overhead is dark apart from NAV & LOGO, the signs and the blue APU and RCDR GND CTL buttons, and both EFIS panels show QNH 1015.

Use this photo as the target: after the steps below, your overhead should be just as dark. It was taken in cruise, so the APU is off and the outside lights differ; at the gate the blue APU buttons stay on, and so does RCDR GND CTL once you press it.

4. MCDU programming

Program MCDU 1 (left side of the pedestal) in the order DATA, INIT A, F PLN, RAD NAV, INIT B, PERF, then set the FCU and brief the takeoff. Airbus pilots remember this as DIFRIPS (the S is SEC F PLN, optional); the entries below match the trainer step for step.

Done when: F PLN runs from 35L through GINLI, ERTAS, BKZ and IST into the ILS to 35R with no gap, PERF TAKE OFF shows 137, 138 and 142, the FMA shows 1FD2, and the takeoff is briefed.

5. Before pushback, pushback and engine start

Close the aircraft, switch to APU power, push back, then start engine 2 and engine 1 with APU air. The start itself is automatic.

Done when: both engines run steadily and ENG MODE is back at NORM, with the tug gone.

Next: 6. After start

6. After start

Turn off APU air and the APU, arm the spoilers, set takeoff flaps and trim, and check the ECAM is clear.

Done when: the APU is off, the spoilers are armed, flaps 1+F and the trim are set, and the ECAM shows no amber message.

Next: 7. Taxi out to runway 35L

7. Taxi out to runway 35L

Taxi slowly on idle thrust: under 20 kt on straight lines, under 10 kt in turns. Istanbul taxi routes are long, often 10 to 30 minutes, so be patient.

Done when: you are stopped short of runway 35L with T.O CONFIG NORMAL, the T.O MEMO all green (CABIN may stay blue) and the takeoff briefing confirmed.

Next: 8. Line up and takeoff

8. Line up and takeoff

TCAS and strobe on, line up, landing lights on for the takeoff, set thrust in two steps, track the centre line with the pedals, rotate at VR toward 15° nose up, gear up, autopilot on.

Done when: gear and flaps are up, AP1 is on and the FMA reads THR CLB, CLB, NAV.

Lining up

Takeoff roll

Climb out

Next: 9. Climb to FL150

9. Climb to FL150

Managed climb does the flying. Your jobs: keep the FCU altitude above you, do the 10,000 ft items, and switch the altimeters to STD at 12,000 ft.

Done when: the FMA shows ALT CRZ at FL150 and both altimeters show STD.

Next: 10. Cruise: 3 minutes at FL150

10. Cruise: 3 minutes at FL150

The cruise lasts about 3 minutes, from the top of climb to the top of descent around ERTAS. That is short, so do the weather and briefing lists below at the gate before pushback, or pause the sim when you level off. The trainer calls this approach preparation WARNBIC: Weather, Approach, Radios, Nav, Briefing, Items, Checklist.

Done when: the arrival is checked, autobrake LO is armed, the seat belt signs are on and you have briefed the approach.

Check the cruise

Weather and arrival

Cockpit and briefing

Next: 11. Descent

11. Descent

At the T/D arrow on the ND, set a lower FCU altitude and push the ALT knob. Managed descent follows the path the FMS built backwards from the runway, down to 3,000 ft and 220 kt at CF35R.

Done when: both altimeters show QNH 1015 and you are past IST, descending toward 3,000 ft at CF35R.

Next: 12. ILS approach to 35R

12. ILS approach to 35R

Activate the approach phase and set up the ILS, press APPR after the turn at IST, slow down while adding flaps one step at a time, then gear down and landing flaps on the glideslope. Be fully set up by 1,000 ft above the runway.

Done when: at 1,000 ft above the runway you are on the localizer and glideslope with gear down, flaps FULL and speed at VAPP.

Approach phase and ILS

Slowing down

Glideslope and final checks

Next: 13. Landing

13. Landing

For a first flight, let the autoland do it and just handle thrust and reversers. Once that feels easy, fly the last 1,000 ft by hand.

Done when: you are at taxi speed on the runway with the reversers stowed and the autopilot off.

Option A: autoland

Option B: manual landing

After touchdown (both options)

Next: 15. After landing and taxi back to the gate

14. Go around (if needed)

Not set up by 1,000 ft, off the centre line, too fast, or anything feels wrong: go around. It is a normal manoeuvre, not a failure.

Done when: you are level at 4,000 ft on 353° with gear and flaps up, ready for another try.

Another try: 12. ILS approach to 35R

15. After landing and taxi back to the gate

Once the whole aircraft is past the runway holding lines, clean it up, start the APU, then taxi back to the gate on your flight card along the route you planned before pushback.

Done when: the aircraft stands on the STOP mark at your gate.

Clean up (clear of the runway)

Taxi in

Next: 16. Parking and securing

16. Parking and securing

Set the brake, shut the engines down on APU power, then either stay powered for the next flight or go all the way back to cold and dark.

Done when: the engines are off and the beacon is dark, with the aircraft on APU or ground power; or everything is dark if you secure it.

Parking

Flight complete. Staying powered for another flight? Stop here and start again at section 3.

Securing (back to cold and dark)

A330 differences

The A330 shares the A320's cockpit logic: FCU, FMA, MCDU pages, ECAM and every flow above carry over. These are the places that change.

ItemA320 (this checklist)A330
Weights and fuel for this flightZFW 58.0 t, block 5.0 tZFW about 150 t, block about 8 t; take both from your EFB
INIT B weight entryZFW/ZFWCGRead the field label: some versions want ZFWCG/ZFW, CG first
Ground powerOne EXT PWR buttonEXT A and EXT B buttons for two ground power plugs; switch on each that shows AVAIL
HydraulicsPTU links green and yellowNo PTU. Green is driven by both engines, blue by engine 1, yellow by engine 2, plus an electric pump per system
Fuel panelSix pumpsMore pumps, standby pumps and a trim tank. Same rule: no OFF lights, mode selectors in AUTO
Takeoff flaps1 (CONF 1+F)1 or 2, whichever the EFB gives
RotationToward 15°Same 3° per second, but follow the FD pitch bar rather than a fixed number; the long A330 has less tail clearance
TaxiNormal turns60 m wingspan and the nosewheel far behind you: turn later, keep the main gear on the centre line, park at a wide body stand
ClimbBriskSlower when heavy; the divide by 7 cruise rule still works
LandingFlaps FULLFlaps FULL (3 is also approved); VAPP comes from PERF APPR as on the A320

Pick an A330 capable gate at the start; at Istanbul, wide body aircraft use the larger contact or remote stands, and your sim's parking list shows which ones fit.

Beginner traps and quick fixes

Most first flight problems come from one of these. Read the FMA first; it tells you what the aircraft is actually doing.

What you seeWhyFix
Aircraft will not move on the groundPARK BRK still ON, or chocks still inRelease the brake; remove chocks in the EFB or IOS
Nosewheel will not steerTug still connected (NW STRG DISC), A/SKID & N/W STRG off, or no tiller assignedWait for the tug, switch it ON, map a tiller axis
Engine will not startNo APU BLEED, or ENG MODE not at IGN/STARTAPU BLEED ON, mode IGN/START, then the master
LVR CLB flashing after takeoffThrust levers still in FLX or TOGAPull them back to the CL detent
Aircraft levels off and will not climbFCU altitude reached (FMA shows ALT)Turn ALT higher and push it
Speed wanders, no A/THR on the FMAAutothrust disconnectedLevers in CL, press A/THR on the FCU
Amber THR LK on the FMAAutothrust turned off with levers in CL; thrust is frozenMove the levers to set thrust, or press A/THR again
Aircraft flies straight past the routeF PLN DISCONTINUITY ahead, or HDG mode instead of NAVClear the discontinuity; push the HDG knob for NAV
No descent at T/D, DECELERATE shownALT knob not pushedSet the lower altitude and push ALT
Descent stops earlyFCU altitude or an altitude constraint reachedLower the FCU altitude and push ALT
APPR will not captureILS not tuned, LS off, or not heading toward the localizerCheck RAD NAV, press LS, turn toward the localizer, press APPR again
Flaps will not extend or overspeed warningFaster than the amber = limit on the speed tapeSlow down first: pull SPD and select lower, or use the speed brake
QNH or STD flashing on the PFDAltimeter not changed at 12,000 ft or at the transition levelPull BARO for STD climbing, push for QNH descending
Warning tone will not stop after autopilot offDisconnect not acknowledgedPress the red sidestick button a second time
FORMAT ERROR or NOT ALLOWED on the MCDUWrong format, field or flight phaseCLR and retype; check the example in section 4

Next step: real Istanbul procedures

Once the trainer loop feels easy, fly the same trip with a real departure and arrival, as airline crews do. Only section 4 and the descent change; the rest of this checklist stays as written.

Departure: a SID from 35L

Arrival: point merge STAR to ILS 35R

Istanbul arrivals use point merge STARs: you fly a level arc around a merge point (SADIK, IMREN, DIVDI or INSTA), then a short transition to the ILS, normally level at 4,000 ft until the glideslope for 35R.

Point merge shortcut

The STAR ends in a curved arc flown level around a merge point (for 35R, SADIK). Real ATC sends you direct to that point when there is a gap in traffic. Offline, do it yourself once you are on the arc and at its level:

The arc keeps everyone at the same distance from SADIK, so ATC can space aircraft by choosing when to send each one direct. Offline you choose the moment yourself; turning direct early simply makes the flight shorter.
